subject: Request: one-off sandbox grant for FastStart Labs — velocity anomaly
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: fraud-ops@redwood.com; aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: one-off sandbox grant for FastStart Labs — velocity anomaly

Hi team,

Quick one — Alicia (FastStart Labs) is asking for a sandbox top-up they say is to run a partner PoC ahead of a commercial evaluation. We see a cluster of 14 signups tied to this org over the past 36 hours that look...weird. Attached are the raw signup CSV and an IP summary (signup-export.csv, ip-trace-summary.txt).

Why I'm asking: sales needs a small, one-off grant to run a 30-minute demo next Tues; Alicia says procurement signoff is ~48hrs after the demo. If we block them now we risk losing momentum.

Asks: can fraud confirm if this is likely legitimate (same org/procurement contact) vs a rotating disposable-domain/ISP cluster? If low risk, can we approve a limited credit issuance (5k token-equivalent) with throttles?

Context: deal HS-34219 (HubSpot link below). Alicia is the listed contact. Demo is scheduled 2026-11-11.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise SDR, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0126

Attachments: signup-export.csv (CSV stub), ip-trace-summary.txt (plain-text stub)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com; fraud-ops@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-07T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: one-off sandbox grant for FastStart Labs — velocity anomaly

Priya — thanks for the packet. Quick summary after an initial triage:
- Risk score: 0.64 (moderate-high) based on our signup heuristics.
- Flags observed: 9/14 accounts show disposable-email domains (mailinator-style), 7/14 share overlapping device fingerprint hashes, and IPs resolve to two small cloud-hosting ranges with frequent rotation.
- Behavioral signal: token consumption patterns across the cohort are very bursty (short high-throughput requests), consistent with scripted load rather than organic exploration.

That said, two accounts are tied to "alicia@faststart.ai" and the HubSpot contact references the same company domain. The presence of a real corporate domain mixed with throwaway addresses suggests either a batch onboarding attempt with some legitimate users or a partner-run integration test that used disposable emails for automation.

Recommendation: do not issue full credits to all account artifacts. If Sales wants to proceed, we can approve a constrained, auditable grant to the verified Alicia account only (5000 tokens), with the following controls:
1) Apply rate limits (50 tokens/minute) and per-minute burst cap.
2) Mark all cohort accounts for 14-day monitoring and auto-revoke on heuristic escalation.
3) Require Sales to confirm the corporate billing domain and provide a short written attestation from Alicia.
4) File Ops ticket to apply grant to a single account id and set a revocation playbook.

I'll open JIRA-OPS-7216 and set a watch. If you want, we can fast-track a manual grant but only after Alicia confirms via corporate email and we bind throttles.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Fraud Detection Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Looping in from Sales Ops POV — agreed with Aditya's precautions. One procedural note: if we make an exception, let's formalize it so it's auditable for renewals/discounts later. My suggestions:
- Approve one-time 5k token grant to alicia@faststart.ai only.
- Create a short exception record in SFDC (reason: partner PoC, PO submitted, JIRA-OPS-7216) and tag the account as "manual-grant-audit".
- Require that the grant be single-account and time-limited (expires in 14 days). If activity looks automated (Aditya's heuristics), Ops to revoke immediately.

Priya — if you can get Alicia to send the PO from a corporate domain and reply to this thread confirming, I'll trigger the SFDC record and alert Ops to apply the grant with throttles.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com; ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09T17:02:00-08:00
Subject: Final: conditional grant approved (alicia@faststart.ai) — controls applied

Priya/Ben — finalizing. Based on the PO confirmation (forwarded), phone confirmation, and HubSpot crosscheck, fraud signs are acceptable for a restricted, auditable trial grant. Actions taken: 
1) Approved 5,000-token sandbox grant to user account: alicia@faststart.ai (expires 2026-11-23).
2) Rate limiting enforced: 50 tokens/minute, 200 tokens/hour burst cap.
3) Cohort accounts added to watchlist; automated revocation rules set (JIRA-OPS-7216).
4) Ops ticket created to attach grant and monitor usage dashboard; alerts sent to fraud-ops and sales-ops channels.

Countermeasures: if any of the cohort accounts (>3) exceed defined heuristics (high fingerprint overlap, rapid-sequence session creation, or >3 distinct cloud-proxy ASNs), we revoke the grant immediately and block related accounts.

I'll leave monitoring on for 14 days and will escalate if anything looks off. Priya — please confirm receipt of grant to Alicia and retain the PO in the HubSpot deal.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
